Rituximab in stiff person syndrome
P.J. Garcia-Ruiz, J. del Val, A. Herranz, S. Bellido, M.A. Aranda
(Madrid, Spain)
Objective: To report a case of woman with stiff person syndrome
and clinical respose to rituximab therapy.
Background: Stiff person syndrome (SPS) is characterised by stiff-
ness and paroxysmal painful spams, predominantly, in axial muscles.
SPS is an infrequent progressive autoimmune disease of the central
nervous system, associated with anti-GAD antibodies; and other anti-
bodies in paraneoplastic cases. Treatment is based on GABA enhanc-
ing drugs and inmunomodulatory therapies (plasmapheresis, inmuno-
globulin and citotoxic agents) with varying success. Rituximab, an
anti-CD20 antibody, has shown efﬁcacy in any cases reports.
Methods: A 32-year-old female was diagnosed two years ago
based on clinical and electromyography criteria, with anti-GAD posi-
tivity. She was treated with diazepam, gabapentine, tizanidine, corti-
costeroids and periodic inmunoglobulin; with partial and transient
improvement. Rituximab was proposed.
Results: Rituximab was administered at a dose of 1000 mg.
Twenty days after infusio´n the stiffness began to improve, especially
painful spams. This improvement persists three months after treat-
ment. The anti-GAD plasmatic levels did not fall during follow-up.
Conclusions: Rituximab may be effective in the treatment of SPS.
Further studies are needed to establish the efﬁcacy, adverse events
and duration of the effects of rituximab in the treatment of SPS.
